entries.title: Darkshore
body: Darkshore is a long, misty coast on the north-western edge of Kalimdor, a strip of dark forest and grey beaches between the mountains and the sea. Before the Sundering it lay on the shore of the Well of Eternity, and the ruins of Highborne towns still stand among its trees. Its only real town is Auberdine, the harbour that links the night elves on Teldrassil with the mainland and with the human and dwarven kingdoms across the sea.

The forest is sick. Beyond the eastern mountains lies Felwood, and its corruption has crept down the rivers into Darkshore: the thistle bears have gone rabid, the Blackwood furbolgs have turned hostile, and satyrs feed on the magic of the old ruins. Greymist murlocs and naga hold the beaches, and great sea creatures keep washing up dead on the shore.

Older enemies have returned too. Cultists of the Twilight's Hammer search the ruins for forgotten power, and a coven of warlocks called the Cult of the Dark Strand has gathered at a Highborne tower in the north. The druids, Sentinels and townsfolk of Auberdine are few, and they welcome any help that comes off the boats.
sources: page texts 358, 364 (towns on the shore of the Well of Eternity)
pre-Cataclysm lore: Auberdine harbour and its boat to Menethil Harbor

entries.title: Auberdine
body: A night elf village on Darkshore's western coast, built of pale wood around a moonwell and an inn. Its docks send ferries to Rut'theran Village at the foot of Teldrassil and ships south to Menethil Harbor, and the hippogryph master Caylais Moonfeather keeps flights going to the World Tree. Dwarven smiths, miners and archaeologists of the Explorers' League have settled here alongside the elves.

The village is run by its elder, Thundris Windweaver, and a village council, and defended by a handful of Sentinels under Elissa Starbreeze and Glynda Nal'Shea. It is not an easy place to live. Murlocs have sunk ships off the coast, the forest around the village is turning against it, and some of its people have already left for the safer lands of the Alliance.
sources: quest 2139 reward text (people leaving for fortified lands)
creatures 3841 Caylais Moonfeather, 6737 Innkeeper Shaussiy, 6297-6301 dwarven smiths and miners, 2913 Archaeologist Hollee

entries.title: Ameth'Aran
body: The ruins of a Highborne town east of the main road, south of Auberdine. In the days of Queen Azshara its people practised powerful magic freely here, and two great tablets among the stones still tell of its founding and its fall.

The town's people never truly left. Their cursed and wailing spirits walk the ruins, still carrying the magical implements of their old lives, and they drive off anyone who comes to read the tablets. In the middle of the ruins an ancient flame, blue in colour, burns as it has since before the Sundering.
sources: creatures 2176 Cursed Highborne, 2177 Writhing Highborne, 2178 Wailing Highborne

entries.title: Bashal'Aran
body: The twin of Ameth'Aran, a second ruined Highborne town to the east of Auberdine. Sprites, grells and satyrs have moved into it, and they feed on the magic that still lingers among the stones, growing stronger the longer they stay.

There is one place they will not go. On a small bluff at the western edge of the ruins stands a shrine wrapped in a strange blue light. It is a prison, and its prisoner, the spirit of the Highborne mage Asterion, has stared out between its pillars for more than a thousand years.
sources: creatures 2189 Vile Sprite, 2190 Wild Grell, 2212 Deth'ryll Satyr

entries.title: Tower of Althalaxx
body: A tall elven tower in the north-east of Darkshore, standing apart from the old towns. Ten thousand years ago it was the home of Athrikus Narassin, the Highborne who governed Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran for Azshara.

Warlocks have taken it over, a cult that calls itself the Dark Strand, with a satyr among their number. The weaker cultists keep to the grounds; the strongest are inside. Balthule Shadowstrike, sent from Auberdine to watch the tower, has not dared to leave his post in case he misses something.
sources: page texts 364, 361, 437 (Balthule's letter, a foul satyr)
creatures 2336 Dark Strand Fanatic, 3662 Delmanis the Hated

entries.title: Ruins of Mathystra
body: Broken walls and toppled stones at Darkshore's northern end, all that remains of Mathystra, once a great stronghold of the elves. Its glory has faded, but fragments of its magic remain in the relics scattered in the grass.

Others have found the place first. Naga of the Stormscale have come ashore and made the ruins their own, and the Twilight's Hammer covets the old elven magic buried here. The Ancients of the Grove want the relics studied before the cult can make use of them.

entries.title: Cliffspring Falls
body: A waterfall in the mountains east and a little north of Auberdine. A cave behind the falling water is the only place where certain rare mushrooms grow, and the alchemist Barithras Moonshade used to gather them there.

The Ancients warned him away. They sensed a new evil hiding in the cave, and they were right: naga and thugs of the Twilight's Hammer have made it a den. That the two should turn up together, so far from the sea's depths, troubles Onu more than either would alone.
sources: creatures 2339 Twilight Thug, 7017 Lord Sinslayer, 2179 Stormscale Wave Rider

entries.title: Cliffspring River
body: The river that runs down from the mountains north of Auberdine and empties into the Mist's Edge. A bridge crosses it just above its first waterfall.

Its water is going bad. Blackwood furbolgs camp along its upper course, but Thundris Windweaver believes they are only the nearest cause of the taint, not the root of it. Samples drawn from the pool below the falls grow more putrid by the week, and the village fears the foul water will soon wash down to Auberdine itself.

entries.title: Grove of the Ancients
body: A grove close under the mountains in southern Darkshore, home to living trees, the Ancients, who are among the night elves' oldest and wisest allies. A few elves keep a small post among them.

The Ancients feel what moves through the forest, and their warnings carry weight in Auberdine. Onu, an Ancient of Lore, watches over the grove. Druids pass through on the road south as well, among them Kerlonian Evershade, a Druid of the Claw so recently woken from the Emerald Dream that he keeps nodding off on his way to Ashenvale.

entries.title: The Master's Glaive
body: A huge blade driven deep into the earth in southern Darkshore. The Ancients say it marks the place where one of the old lords of the earth fell long ago, impaled by the glaive. The lord is long dead, but slivers of his power may linger in the ground.

The Twilight's Hammer has set up camp around it. Their disciples guard a tome written in an ancient hand, and the dryad Therylune, who wandered too close, had to hide among the rocks until someone came to lead her out.

entries.title: Remtravel's Excavation
body: A dig site in the south of Darkshore run by Prospector Remtravel of the Explorers' League, a dwarf famous at the Ironforge academy for his discoveries. His team uncovered signs of a great and ancient society here.

Then the golems came. Stone creatures burst out of the ground and overran the site, and his assistant Hollee ran to Auberdine for help. Remtravel stayed, apparently without noticing, still looking for his stone brush and the fossil he had promised the League.

entries.title: Blackwood Den
body: A cave in southern Darkshore, below the road, held by the strongest of the Blackwood furbolgs. Their ursas and shamans guard it.

The druid Volcor was wounded by the furbolgs and took shelter deep inside, where he could neither fight his way out alone nor be found by his friends. His companion Grimclaw waited by the road outside and carried word of him to Auberdine.

entries.title: Mist's Edge
body: The strait between Darkshore and Teldrassil, crossed every day by the ferries and hippogryphs from Auberdine. Its waters are cold and grey, and the Cliffspring River empties into it from the north.

The sea here has turned dangerous. Greymist murlocs camp along the beaches and raid the boats, and two ships, the Silver Dawning and the Mist Veil, lie wrecked off the coast north of Auberdine with their captains' lockboxes still aboard. Giant threshers and sea turtles keep beaching themselves on the shore, and nobody yet knows why.
sources: quest 4723 description (coast of the Mist's Edge)
quest 4762 description (Cliffspring River empties into the Mist's Edge)
quest 1141 (no boats going out since the murlocs)

entries.title: Thundris Windweaver
body: The elder of Auberdine, who looks after the everyday affairs of the village and is known for his sound and fair judgement. He believes dark forces are pressing in on every side and that the whole village must keep watch.

Thundris knows corruption when he sees it. He has seen Felwood's taint before, and he traces the poison in the Cliffspring River back over the mountains to it. He is just as wary of the past: he wants the relics carried by the Highborne spirits of Ameth'Aran gathered up and destroyed, so their magic can never be used again.

entries.title: Onu
body: An Ancient of Lore of the Grove of the Ancients, a great tree who speaks slowly and only after long thought. Those who seek him out are told to listen to what the wind whispers.

Onu was the first to put the Twilight's Hammer's presence in Darkshore together with the naga's. He sends trusted helpers to the Master's Glaive and the Ruins of Mathystra, gives them phials of scrying so they can speak to him from afar, and meditates on what the cult intends.

entries.title: Asterion
body: A Highborne mage who lived in Bashal'Aran when the Well of Eternity still stood, second only to the governor Athrikus Narassin. Something went wrong between them, and Athrikus bound Asterion's spirit to a shrine with a moonstone seal.

He spent more than a thousand years in that prison, sharp-tongued and half afraid he had gone mad. The seal was found on one of the satyrs of Bashal'Aran and destroyed in the ancient flame of Ameth'Aran, and Asterion is free at last. His first thought is of the world that has changed beyond recognition; his second is of vengeance on his former master, whom he senses is still alive.
sources: quests 954, 955, 956, 957 descriptions, progress and reward texts
item 5338 Ancient Moonstone Seal dropped by creature 2212 Deth'ryll Satyr

entries.title: Athrikus Narassin
body: A Highborne favoured by Queen Azshara, who placed him over Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran. When the War of the Ancients brought the towns down, he came to the people of Ameth'Aran with a spell he said would protect them and give them eternal life. Their spirits still haunt the ruins.

Athrikus survived the Sundering and leads the Cult of the Dark Strand from the top of his old tower, drawing power from soul gems that hold trapped Highborne souls. With those gems broken, he waits among his strongest warlocks.

entries.title: Cerellean Whiteclaw
body: A druid of Auberdine who loved Anaya Dawnrunner of Ameth'Aran before the Sundering. After the battles at the Well of Eternity he heard that the town had fallen and that she was dead, and he followed Malfurion Stormrage into the long sleep of the druids with that grief still with him.

Thousands of years later, wandering the woods half in a daze, he came to the ruins and saw Anaya's haunted spirit among them. He knows she must be released, but he cannot bring himself to raise a hand against her, and he asks someone else to do it and bring back her pendant.
sources: quest 963 description, progress and reward texts

entries.title: Terenthis
body: A druid of the Cenarion Circle who has come to Auberdine to learn how far the fel moss has spread. Some of his brethren on Teldrassil had to be rescued from corrupted furbolgs, and he has vowed to stop such things happening again.

His scouts found the Blackwood furbolgs south of Auberdine already corrupted, and close enough to threaten the village. Terenthis does not like ordering the killing of forest creatures, but until a cure is found he believes there is no other choice.

entries.title: Volcor and Grimclaw
body: Volcor is a friend of Terenthis who fell foul of the Blackwood furbolgs and lay hurt in their den. His faithful companion Grimclaw found Terenthis and brought the news, then went back to wait beside the road.

Terenthis made an enchanted moonstalker cloak to let a rescuer slip past the furbolgs unseen. Once found, Volcor offered a choice: sneak out under the cloak's magic, or fight down to the road and deal with the furbolgs once and for all.

entries.title: Tharnariun Treetender
body: A druid of Auberdine who has made the thistle bears his charge. Once noble animals, they have been struck by a sickness that leaves them rabid and destructive, and Tharnariun hoped to cure them, catching sick bears in a trap of light that calms them long enough to lead them home.

The cure failed. Grieving, he ordered the sick bears culled, and then the death of the Den Mother in her cave near Bashal'Aran, from which the rabid bears keep coming. He says plainly that many in Darkshore are not equal to the hardships of their new home.

entries.title: Wizbang Cranktoggle
body: A gnome inventor in Auberdine who has scattered his buzzboxes up and down the coast: lever-topped machines that let people talk to each other over long distances. Each needs constant repair, and he cleverly placed each one beside the creatures whose parts it needs, from crawler legs to thistle bear scalps.

The longer anyone talks to him through the boxes, the less sober he sounds. The buzzboxes also brew and distil liquor, a trade the night elves will not tolerate in their towns, and Wizbang hides a little of his best stock in them for whoever keeps them running.

entries.title: Murkdeep
body: A murloc of the Greymist tribe who guards a hutted camp on the water south of Auberdine. The village council holds him responsible for the death of at least one Sentinel, and suspects him of sinking two cargo ships off the coast.
The council has posted a bounty on him, payable by Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea. Few things would let the people of Auberdine sleep more easily than news of his death.

entries.title: Gelkak Gyromast
body: A self-styled pirate captain stranded on Darkshore's far northern shore after threshadons sank his ship. He talks like a sea dog and calls everyone landlubber.

Gelkak's pride is his first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100, a fighting machine stamped as his property. Its key broke on the rocks when he washed ashore, and crawlers, foreststriders and murlocs carried off the pieces. Once the machine is working again, he means to turn it on the murlocs.

entries.title: The Twin Towns
body: Long ago the night elves, who called themselves the children of the stars, built their homes on the shores of the Well of Eternity, where they believed Elune herself rested. Of the towns on the shore that later became Darkshore, Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran were the finest, touched by Queen Azshara's own hand and home to her favoured Highborne.

Azshara gave the towns to Athrikus Narassin, who spent most of his days in the Tower of Althalaxx, and his second, the mage Asterion, saw to their people. The towns prospered while the world around them slid into madness.

When the War of the Ancients came, the forest was torn up and the towns fell. As Ameth'Aran lay in ruins, Athrikus offered its survivors a spell of protection and eternal life against the Sundering to come. The Highborne spirits that wander its stones today show what that promise was worth.

entries.title: Washed Ashore
body: Great sea creatures have always beached themselves on Darkshore now and then, but lately they come ashore in alarming numbers. The Temple of the Moon in Darnassus sent Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde to Auberdine to find out why, and the Explorers' League tried to study one of the carcasses before murlocs chased them off.

The remains raise more questions than they answer. Some are threshers far larger than any native to these waters; others are gentle sea mammals and turtles from the seas around Teldrassil, which once swam in great numbers about the roots of Nordrassil and have grown scarcer since the new tree was planted. Gwennyth wonders whether they are fleeing the World Tree.
Some of the turtles carried naga harness and cargo, marked with naga script, which explains the naga now on Darkshore's northern beaches but not what they want.
sources: quest 6343 (fish near Teldrassil larger than on the mainland)

entries.title: The Taint from Felwood
body: Over the mountains east of Darkshore lies Felwood, a forest corrupted by demons, and its sickness is spreading west. The Cliffspring River is fouling, the thistle bears have gone rabid, and the Blackwood furbolgs, once friends of the elves, attack anyone near their camps.

The druids of Auberdine have learned that the furbolgs do not fall alone. Satyrs work their corruption through talismans, and when a cleansing offering of moonwell water and furbolg food briefly freed some of the Blackwood, a satyr corruptor came out of hiding to reclaim them.
Every victory so far has been small. No cure has been found for the bears or the furbolgs, and the elves can only slow the corruption until one is.

entries.title: The Twilight's Hammer
body: The Twilight's Hammer fought as an orcish clan in the Second War, and today it is a cult that worships the old lords of the earth, ancient powers defeated and imprisoned long ago. Its members have appeared in Darkshore at the Master's Glaive, in the cave behind Cliffspring Falls and around the Ruins of Mathystra.

A page torn from a tome at their camp turned out to be part of an ancient text written by elves, cursed and tainted by the cult's own magic. The Ancients believe the Twilight's Hammer means to use the old magic of the elves to call its masters back into the world, and are racing to understand that magic first.
sources: pre-Cataclysm lore: the Twilight's Hammer clan and its Old God worship

entries.title: The Cult of the Dark Strand
body: When Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze sent Balthule Shadowstrike to watch the Tower of Althalaxx, he found it full of warlocks whose scrolls named them the Cult of the Dark Strand, a group nobody had heard of. Balthule's master, the paladin Delgren the Purifier at Maestra's Post in Ashenvale, had suspected such a gathering.

Delgren traced the cult's strength to soul gems holding trapped Highborne souls, kept at Night Run and Satyrnaar in Ashenvale, and to its dealings with the orc warlock Ilkrud Magthrull of the Fire Scar Shrine. Behind it all stood Athrikus Narassin, the ancient Highborne lord of the tower.

entries.title: The Red Crystal
body: Moonkin roam the woods east of Auberdine in growing numbers. They were once thought gentle, almost mystical creatures, and some elves still revere them, but these attack on sight. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea learned they were gathering around a large red crystal on Darkshore's eastern mountainside.

Moonwell water poured over the crystal turned its surface clear for a moment, revealing fragments of bone and half of a humanoid jawbone sealed inside. Nobody knows what it is. Glynda suspects a link to Felwood, just over the mountains, and has taken the question to the village council.
